the 5' regulatory sequence we have cloned and characterized from the genomic library of Brassic campestris is a recombinant product and is likely to have arisen through gene conversion between the two napin gene family members.

the promoter region of one of the 1.2S seed-specific albumin-coding genes from Brassica campestis is apparently a recombinant of two different promoters of two different napin genes.

the cloning and sequencing of a recombinant promoter from a genomic library of B. campestris, and the evolutionary significance of this fact.
the isolation of the 5'-flanking regulatory region of one of the napin-coding genes from a genomic library of B. campestris and its sequence analysis.
the cloning and sequencing of a 2S albumins gene promoter and the possible evolutionary significance of its origin.

the 5' upstream regulatory region of napin gene from B. campestris is a recombinant product and that the evolution of Brassica species has been through gene duplication and gene rearrangement.

the 2S seed storage protein genes in the Brassica genus evolved from a common ancestor, through gene duplication and recombinational events, which resulted in the generation of a large family of genes in the present day Brassica species.

we have isolated a recombinant promoter sequence of the napin family of 2S albumins and that the recombinant promoter is a double crossover between two napin gene family members.

gene duplication and recombined products may be a major mechanism of evolution.
